title: Federated learning and digital twins for lifecycle optimization in Urban building renewal
domain: Building geometry and staged renovation; S1 enabling inputs and lifecycle intervention planning
reason: Substantive three-layer building DT with simulated sensing/BIM updates, behavioral posterior uncertainty and explicit robustness/calibration evaluation. Eligible under enabling geometry/renewal scope; not a full material-stock/recovery chain.
DTstatus: Simulation-based physical/digital/intelligence architecture; bidirectional sensor-policy loop and quarterly geometric updates; not field deployment
Umechanism: Bayesian variational inference for epistemic/aleatoric uncertainty; residual/interval thresholds trigger retraining/fallback; Gaussian sensor noise/dropout and occupancy sensitivity; nominal95% interval empirical94.7% coverage reported
locators: PDF pp.5–7 Fig.1–3 architecture; pp.9–11 methods; p.20 Fig.13 calibration/results; pp.22–24 discussion/limitations
evidence: p.10 describes ray-cast synthetic LiDAR and variational Bayesian behavior model; p.20 reports94.7% empirical coverage for nominal95% intervals.
limits: 60-building synthetic EnergyPlus testbed; no demonstrated transfer of material-quantity/recoverability distributions. Real-world validity requires pilot deployment. Reported empirical coverage pertains simulated environment.
continuity: No demonstrated S1–S5 continuous propagation; local state prediction/update feedback only
review_extent: Actual PDF methods, relevant results and limitations read at listed pages; not a cover-to-cover/supplement audit

title: Prediction and optimization of structural performance of prefabricated bridges based on physical information neural network (PINN) and BlM
domain: Prefabricated bridge structures; not building material-chain application
reason: Full text confirms bridge-only geometry/material-to-PINN performance optimization. Excluded from building-domain intersection despite substantive BIM integration and measured errors.
DTstatus: BIM-to-PINN geometry/material/load integration with monitoring; digital-twin label used for bridge model
Umechanism: Data/physics residual loss, displacement/stress prediction errors versus sensor tests; stated measurementerror±2%; no propagated probability model established
locators: PDF p.6 section3.1; p.8 section3.2; p.14 Table1; p.15 Tables2–3; p.18 conclusion
evidence: p.15 reports static displacement prediction errors0.43–0.83% and live-load stress errors0.66–1.63% for three bridge models.
limits: Bridge-specific; deterministic validation error must not be called a calibrated uncertainty distribution. Additional sensors proposed for future work.
complement: Potential general DT/model validation comparison only; not a selected S-U/SDT building study
review_extent: Actual PDF methods, relevant results and limitations read at listed pages; not a cover-to-cover/supplement audit

title: Indoor point cloud aggregation and simplification based on parsimony of description
reason: Substantive building geometry/error analysis, but DT is an anticipated application in abstract/conclusion, not a developed DT architecture or connection. Does not meet triple-intersection DT criterion.
DTstatus: DT application mentioned; actual architecture is four-module point-cloud simplification/aggregation/corpus/optimization pipeline
Umechanism: Noise/outlier filtering, voxel occupancy probabilities, data-fitting/coverage loss; per-class precision/recall/F1 against annotation and parameter sensitivity. Classification probabilities not independently calibrated uncertainty.
locators: PDF pp.4–6 sections3.1–3.3; p.8 training; p.11 Table2 and section4.3; pp.15–17 discussion/conclusion
evidence: p.11 Table2 reports walls F1=84.1%, windows29.9%, doors33.0%; p.16 attributes opening failures to geometric scale,sensor-material interaction,and representation.
limits: Planar primitives omit explicit opening topology; curved geometry/occlusions limited. Page17 data-availability statement says no datasets generated/analyzed despite experimental sections; retain as reporting caveat, not proof of invalidity.
complement: Useful S1+error evidence for information loss and geometric representation; retain outside triple Included count
continuity: No downstream stock/flow/impact propagation or operational DT synchronization shown
review_extent: Actual PDF methods, relevant results and limitations read at listed pages; not a cover-to-cover/supplement audit

title: Digital regeneration of historical buildings using UAV photogrammetry and 3D Gaussian splatting for metaverse environments
domain: Heritage building geometry, provenance and representation reliability; S1 enabling workflow
reason: Explicit cloud-to-local heritage DT construction architecture connects UAV/SfM/3DGS to interactive engine, with relative geometric error evaluation and provenance/confidence display. Eligible enabling-geometry evidence; conceptual monitoring kept separate from implemented visualization.
DTstatus: Implemented offline capture-to-interactive digital replica pipeline; temporal monitoring proposed, no validated operational physical synchronization demonstrated
Umechanism: Relative C2C deviation to photogrammetric baseline; held-out rendering metrics; heuristic density/distance softculling; preserved raw baseline and UI distinction of empirical versus inferred assets
locators: PDF pp.3–7 Methods/Fig.2/Eqs.1–3; pp.9–10 Tables1–2/Fig.10; pp.12–13 Discussion/Table4
evidence: p.10 reports meanC2C0.034m SD0.012m and92% within5cm relative baseline; p.6 states no independent TLS; p.12 distinguishes scanned vs inferred historical models.
limits: Both geometric outputs derive from photogrammetry; no absolute metrology. Softculling hides artifacts without recovering missing topology. Proposed2cm temporal alert is not justified by independent change-detection validation; Gaussian covariance is spatial primitive shape, not epistemic uncertainty covariance.
complement: S1+DT accuracy/provenance architecture; not material inventory or recovery-to-impact evidence
continuity: Preserves provenance between capture/rendered interpretation; no S1–S5 uncertainty propagation demonstrated
review_extent: Actual PDF methods, relevant results and limitations read at listed pages; not a cover-to-cover/supplement audit
